# fleet-lighthouse

Know which fleet repos are alive without asking. Zero-dependency Python 3.10+
monitor over the `gh` CLI — the fleet's already-authenticated path.

Also from the oracle1 legacy study (2026-09-26): the old agent's biggest
wound was not knowing which of its sites/repos were down. This is the
instrument that answers in one command.

## Usage

```bash
python -m fleet_lighthouse report --repos quilt-studio,twist-engine
python -m fleet_lighthouse report --org SuperInstance --top 20
python -m fleet_lighthouse report --repos X --since-last   # only what CHANGED
python -m fleet_lighthouse watch --repos X --interval 3600 --rounds 0
python -m fleet_lighthouse report --repos X --fail-on-unhealthy   # CI gate
```

Per repo: staleness (days since last push), open PRs, failing check runs,
open issues, Pages status. `--since-last` diffs against the cached snapshot
(`~/.cache/fleet-lighthouse/last.json`) and only surfaces new/cleared
problems — built for cron, not for scrolling.

Exit codes with `--fail-on-unhealthy`: `0` all healthy, `1` problems found,
`2` usage error.

## First live smoke (2026-09-26)

```
SuperInstance/quilt-studio          1.0d   0 PR   0 fail   1 iss   pages: none
SuperInstance/twist-engine          4.3d   0 PR   8 fail   0 iss   pages: none   ←
SuperInstance/quilt-cortex          0.0d   0 PR   0 fail   1 iss   pages: none
SuperInstance/platonic-randomness  43.9d   0 PR   0 fail   0 iss   pages: none   ← stale
```

It found real signal on its first run. That's the point.
